clue.text: Leader, forceful and obstinately self-willed

parts.note: the head is the leader of a group
forceful means strong

explanation.surface: A forceful leader who is obstinate and will not be told.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stubborn who insists on their own way is described as wilful or intractable, which is this word's sense.

clue.text: Stagger, having no head for wine

indicators.note: having no head says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: to stagger someone is to shock or astound them

explanation.surface: A drinker reels about after too much wine and loses their head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stagger' reads as reeling drunkenly, but here it means astonish; 'having no head' removes the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hock is the British name for German white wine from the Rhine region.

clue.text: Trainer mostly worried about English racecourse

indicators.note: about says the jumbled letters go around the single letter
worried suggests agitated, so the letters are shaken into a new order
mostly says the word loses its final letter, so only most of it is used

explanation.surface: A racehorse trainer is anxious about a big English race meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last R of TRAINER to leave TRAINE; 'worried' rearranges it, and 'about' puts it around E.
explanation.definitionFit: Aintree, near Liverpool, is the English racecourse where the Grand National steeplechase is run.

clue.text: Limitations of concise US poet, it's said

indicators.note: it's said signals that the poet's name is heard, giving a different spelling

parts.note: concise gives short, and the US poet is e e cummings

explanation.surface: Someone remarks on the flaws of a terse American poet.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet e e cummings is famous for lower-case, compressed verse, which suits 'concise'; his surname heard gives the second half.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortcomings are failings or deficiencies, the ways in which something falls short, much like limitations.

clue.text: Satirist, a Bel Air comic, on second

indicators.note: comic here means jokey or knockabout, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A satirist is performing a comedy routine about Bel Air for a second time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comic' reorders A BEL AIR into RABELAI; 'on' simply joins S after it. Bel Air is a wealthy Los Angeles district.
explanation.definitionFit: François Rabelais was the French Renaissance writer of the satirical Gargantua and Pantagruel.

clue.text: Hold naval commander

definitions.meaning: a ... is a wrestling hold applied from behind, as in a full or half ...
Horatio ... was the British admiral who won at Trafalgar

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a wrestling grip and the famous admiral, so each half of the clue defines it.

clue.text: Hard to lose opening argument

indicators.note: to lose opening says the first letter is dropped

parts.note: stiff means hard or rigid

explanation.surface: It is hard to lose the opening debate of a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty quarrel, a minor argument between friends or partners.

clue.text: What bad decision may cause?

parts.note: reads as resentment stirred by a poor choice, but a will is also a testament, so a badly made will may sow family bitterness

explanation.definitionFit: Ill will is hostility or animosity, the bitterness a poorly judged will can provoke among heirs.

clue.text: Following bullock, soldier and dog

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
a bullock is a castrated bull, an ox
a Terrier is a member of the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

explanation.surface: A soldier and his dog walk behind a bullock.
explanation.walkthrough: TERRIER for soldier is British slang for a Territorial Army volunteer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox terrier is a small breed of dog originally used to flush foxes from earths.

clue.text: Shot, clerical dignitary, reportedly at social function

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the cleric's title is heard and spelt like the gun

parts.note: a canon is a senior member of a cathedral's clergy
a ball is a formal dancing party

explanation.surface: A senior cleric is reported to have been shot at a society dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot in the old military sense is solid ammunition, the iron balls fired from a cannon.

clue.text: Message about lake plant

indicators.note: about says the message goes around the single letter

parts.note: a fax is a message sent by telephone line
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A message is sent about a plant growing by a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Flax is the plant grown for linen fibre and linseed.

clue.text: Uncle's first to be embraced by uncommon woman, ninety very soon

indicators.note: to be embraced by says the letter goes inside the jumbled letters
uncommon means unusual, so the letters are put in an unusual order
first says only the opening letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An uncle is hugged by an unusual ninety-year-old woman any time now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncle's first' is just its initial letter, set within the jumbled pool; 'uncommon' is the anagram signal, not a description of the woman.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom meaning imminently, at any moment, which is very soon.

clue.text: Intelligence needed to secure right legal document

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: wit means intelligence or shrewdness

explanation.surface: Brains are needed to secure one's rights with a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: A writ is a formal written court order, a type of legal document.

clue.text: In New York, a sole cooked with onions

indicators.note: cooked suggests the letters are doctored or tampered with, and so rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner in New York orders a sole dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link placing the meal, but it is part of the anagram with NY and A SOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyonnaise describes a dish cooked in the style of Lyon, which means prepared with sliced fried onions.

clue.text: Argue about tiny details in Dalmatian city locks

parts.note: Split is a port city on the Dalmatian coast of Croatia
locks are tresses of hair

explanation.surface: A spotted dog's hair is discussed in great detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dalmatian' suggests the spotted dog, but it means the Dalmatia region of Croatia.
explanation.definitionFit: To split hairs is an idiom for quibbling over trivial distinctions.

clue.text: Prince about to broadcast back in capital

parts.note: re means about or concerning
taken as written

indicators.note: back says the word is read in reverse

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it

explanation.surface: A prince is about to go back on air in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretoria is the administrative capital city of South Africa.

clue.text: Old thriller writer taking stroll by river

parts.note: to amble is to stroll
R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: An old crime author goes for a walk beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Ambler was a British writer of spy thrillers in the mid twentieth century.

clue.text: Slaughter millions as southern race decimated

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for million
taken as written

indicators.note: decimated means devastated or wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reordered

explanation.surface: Millions are killed as a southern people is wiped out.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre is the brutal killing of many people, a slaughter.

clue.text: Spoil one married couple

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: One married couple spoils things for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair something is to damage or weaken it, so to spoil it.

clue.text: Careful having to write about endlessly vulgar time

indicators.note: about says the word for write goes around the shortened word

parts.note: to pen is to write

indicators.note: endlessly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: rude means vulgar or crude

explanation.surface: Someone cautious must write about an endlessly vulgar period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having to' merely joins definition and wordplay; 'endlessly' trims only the vulgar word before it goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Prudent means sensible and cautious, acting with care for the future.

clue.text: Counter clean? Unfortunately it's very sticky

parts.note: a bar is a counter where drinks are served

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone awry, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone wiping a pub counter finds a stubbornly sticky mess.
explanation.definitionFit: A barnacle is a marine crustacean that clings fast to rocks and hulls, famous for adhering.

clue.text: Pirate in element following my lead in sea-roving

indicators.note: following says the element comes after the other pieces

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: lead in says only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: air was one of the four classical elements

explanation.surface: A pirate is in his element when roving the high seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, not a possessive: COR, as in British slang 'cor blimey'.
explanation.definitionFit: A corsair is a pirate, especially one from the Barbary coast.

clue.text: Understand trick

definitions.meaning: to take something in is to grasp or absorb it
to take someone in is to deceive them

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to comprehend and to fool someone.

clue.text: Slim-waisted, rough foreign girl

indicators.note: foreign suggests strange or alien, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A coarse foreign girl with a slender waist.
explanation.definitionFit: An hourglass figure is a woman's shape with a narrow waist, like the timer.

clue.text: Spell 'vase' after bit of tuition

indicators.note: after says the vase comes behind the letter
bit of says only the first letter of the word is taken

parts.note: an urn is a vase

explanation.surface: A lesson in how to spell the word vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spell' looks like spelling, but it means a stint or period, as in 'your turn'.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn is a spell or stint at doing something, one's go.

clue.text: Study prepared? Almost

indicators.note: almost says the word falls one letter short of complete

parts.note: ready means prepared

explanation.surface: Is your study prepared? Almost.
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject is British usage for studying it at university.

clue.text: Thing I encountered upon retirement

indicators.note: retirement means withdrawing or going back, so the word is reversed

parts.note: met means encountered

explanation.surface: A thing I came across after I retired.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single thing or article in a list or collection.

clue.text: In a bad way, PC teenager cut

indicators.note: in a bad way means in a mess, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A teenager hurt in a bad way after a police constable's attack.
explanation.walkthrough: PC is a police constable in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut is a share or proportion of the proceeds, as in taking a percentage.

clue.text: Takes it easy, to some extent, in position

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes a little in their place.
explanation.definitionFit: A site is a location or position where something is or will be placed.

clue.text: Gangland controlled by society

parts.note: under means controlled by, as in under someone's command
the world means society, as in the fashionable world

explanation.surface: Organised crime is run by high society.
explanation.definitionFit: The underworld is the criminal milieu, the realm of organised gangs.
